questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A point on a bow string is in equilibrium. The archer pulls horizontally with 160 N. Two equal string tensions act symmetrically, each at 75° to the horizontal. Calculate the tension in the string.
markPoints: Resolve the two tension forces in the horizontal direction and equate their resultant to 160 N.
Obtain T ≈ 310 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A gamma photon has wavelength 1.25 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Calculate the energy of one photon.
markPoints: Use E = hc/λ (or an equivalent two-step route using f).
Obtain 1.59 × 10⁻¹¹ J.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A transparent layer is 89 nm thick and light in the layer has wavelength 356 nm. Light reflects from the upper and lower surfaces; any equal reflection phase changes can be ignored. Explain why destructive interference occurs.
markPoints: The two reflected waves are in antiphase (180° or π rad apart).
The lower reflection travels an extra 2 × 89 nm = 178 nm.
178 nm is half of 356 nm, so the path difference is λ/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: Sunlight reflected from a lake surface is horizontally polarised, while light reflected from submerged objects is unpolarised. Explain why Polaroid sunglasses can make the submerged objects easier to see. Include the nature of unpolarised light, what polarisation means, and the relative effect of the sunglasses on the two reflected beams.
markPoints: Unpolarised transverse light has oscillations in more than one plane perpendicular to energy transfer.
Polarisation restricts transverse oscillations to one plane.
With the transmission axis chosen appropriately, the horizontally polarised glare is greatly reduced.
The unpolarised light from submerged objects is only partly reduced, so contrast improves.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A free neutron decays. Identify which fundamental interaction is responsible and explain why.
markPoints: Weak nuclear interaction.
The decay involves leptons and/or a change of quark flavour (for example d → u).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A 0.200 g indigestion tablet contains Mg(OH)₂. Add 40.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ HCl in excess. Mg(OH)₂ + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + 2H₂O. The leftover acid needs 29.25 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. Calculate the percentage by mass of Mg(OH)₂.
markPoints: Initial HCl = 0.00800 mol.
NaOH, hence leftover HCl, = 0.002925 mol.
HCl reacting with Mg(OH)₂ = 0.005075 mol.
Mass Mg(OH)₂ ≈ 0.148 g.
Percentage ≈ 74.0%.

questions.subject: Chemistry

markPoints: Record masses accurately / use weighing by difference or quantitative transfer.
Transfer all washings from beaker/stirring rod/container to the volumetric flask.
Use a dropper near the mark and set the bottom of the meniscus on the line.
Stopper and invert several times to mix thoroughly. Any three valid points score.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: A Group 2 nitrate M(NO₃)₂ decomposes: 2M(NO₃)₂ → 2MO + 4NO₂ + O₂. A 0.320 g sample gives 225 cm³ of gas at 450 °C and 101000 Pa. Using R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, determine Mr of M(NO₃)₂ and identify M.
questions.modelAnswer: Convert V = 225 × 10⁻⁶ m³ and T = 723 K. pV = nRT gives 3.78 × 10⁻³ mol gas. 2 mol nitrate give 5 mol gas, so nitrate = 1.51 × 10⁻³ mol. Mr ≈ 211.9. Ar(M) ≈ 87.9, so M is Sr.
markPoints: Correct SI unit conversions.
Find total gas moles using pV=nRT.
Use 2:5 nitrate:gas ratio.
Identify strontium.

Lone-pair–bond-pair repulsion is stronger than bond-pair–bond-pair repulsion, reducing the angle.

questions.prompt: A mass of six tablets is found by subtracting two balance readings. Each reading has uncertainty ±0.005 g, and the mass difference is 2.14 g. Calculate the percentage uncertainty in the tablet mass.
markPoints: Use total absolute uncertainty 0.010 g and divide by 2.14 g, then ×100 to obtain about 0.47%.

questions.prompt: 25.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid is added to some magnesium oxide tablets. Calculate the amount of HCl added.
markPoints: Use n=cV with V=0.0250 dm³ to obtain 0.0500 mol.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.prompt: Six tablets have mass 2.14 g. They react with 25.0 cm³ of 2.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl. The mixture is diluted to 250 cm³. A 25.0 cm³ portion requires 20.38 cm³ of 0.0900 mol dm⁻³ NaOH to neutralise the HCl left over. Given MgO + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂O, calculate the percentage by mass of MgO in the tablets.
markPoints: Initial HCl amount is 0.0500 mol.
Find HCl remaining in the 25.0 cm³ aliquot from the NaOH titre.
Scale the remaining HCl to the full 250 cm³ mixture.
Subtract remaining HCl from initial HCl to find HCl that reacted with MgO.
Use the 2:1 HCl:MgO ratio and Mr(MgO)≈40.3 to find the MgO mass.
Divide MgO mass by 2.14 g and ×100 to obtain about 29.8%.

questions.question: 7(a)
questions.prompt: A triangular field has side lengths 225 m, 234 m and 310 m. Calculate the angle opposite the 225 m side.

questions.prompt: Using the same triangular field with sides 225 m, 234 m and 310 m, suppose each sheep needs 1200 m². Find the maximum whole number of sheep that can be kept in the field.
markPoints: Use 1/2 ab sin C, with a suitable included angle, to find the field area (about 26223 m²).
Divide the area by 1200.
Round down to a maximum of 21 sheep.

Exponentiate to obtain x/y = e³.
Rearrange to x = e³y.

questions.prompt: The specific charge of a hydrogen-3 nucleus is lower than that of the nuclei of the other naturally occurring hydrogen isotopes. Suggest why.
markPoints: The hydrogen isotope nuclei have the same positive nuclear charge / same number of protons.
Hydrogen-3 has the greater nuclear mass, so charge divided by mass is smaller.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: State the principle of moments.
markPoints: For an object in equilibrium, the sum of clockwise moments about a point equals the sum of anticlockwise moments about that point.
Equivalently, the resultant moment about any point is zero.

questions.prompt: Titanium(IV) chloride is formed by TiO₂ + 2C + 2Cl₂ → TiCl₄ + 2CO. Calculate the percentage atom economy for forming TiCl₄.
markPoints: Use atom economy = Mr desired product / total Mr of reactants ×100.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Give one economic advantage of using a process with a high percentage atom economy.
markPoints: Less waste is produced, so less money is lost in unwanted products and/or waste disposal costs are lower.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Write the equation for reducing TiCl₄ with magnesium to form titanium and magnesium chloride.
markPoints: TiCl₄ + 2Mg → Ti + 2MgCl₂.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Explain why magnesium acts as a reducing agent when TiCl₄ is converted to titanium.
markPoints: Magnesium loses electrons / is oxidised.
Those electrons reduce titanium ions; magnesium changes from oxidation state 0 to +2.

markPoints: Use the factor theorem: p(2)=0.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.prompt: Sodium ions Na+ and magnesium ions Mg2+ both have ten electrons. Which ion is smaller? Explain using nuclear charge and electron shielding.
markPoints: The smaller ion is Mg2+.
Both have the same electron arrangement/shielding, but Mg2+ has more protons, so its electrons are attracted more strongly.
questions.modelAnswer: Mg²⁺ is smaller because the two ions are isoelectronic but Mg²⁺ has a higher nuclear charge.

questions.prompt: A negative muon decays by the weak interaction. Name all three particles produced in its ordinary decay.
markPoints: Electron + electron antineutrino + muon neutrino (all three required).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A filament lamp gives a curved current–potential-difference characteristic rather than a straight line. Explain this behaviour using the movement of electrons and the structure and temperature of the metal filament.
markPoints: As the current/potential difference increases, the filament becomes hotter.
The metal lattice ions vibrate more strongly.
Conduction electrons undergo more frequent collisions with the ions.
The lamp's resistance increases, so current is no longer directly proportional to potential difference.
questions.modelAnswer: Greater current heats the filament, causing stronger lattice-ion vibrations and more electron collisions. This raises resistance and causes the nonlinear I–V characteristic.

markPoints: Use the charge divided by the combined proton-and-neutron mass.

markPoints: Pion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.prompt: A deuterium nucleus remains stable because the strong nuclear force changes with nucleon separation. Explain the force's behaviour at distances of roughly a few femtometres and below about 0.5 fm, and how this contributes to stability.
markPoints: The strong nuclear force is attractive at separations of roughly 1–3 fm.
At very short separations (below about 0.5 fm) the force is repulsive.
This balance prevents the proton and neutron separating or collapsing together.
questions.modelAnswer: At typical nuclear separation the strong force is attractive, but it becomes repulsive at very small separations, establishing a stable separation.
